report.summary: Four findings: the PR ships customer emails to an unmodeled third-party analytics endpoint (action_required), plus DFD, dependency and information-asset scope drift.

findings.title: Confidential order data sent to an external analytics service not represented in the model

model_excerpt.quote: data_flow_diagram_v2 "checkout" { process "Web App"; external_element "Customer"; data_store "Orders Database" }

evidence.note: Payload includes "email": o.CustomerEmail and order amount
http.Post sends the payload to the third-party collector
Store.Create now calls publishAnalytics(o) on every order creation

relevance.justification: The model's only egress from Web App is the SQL flow to the Orders Database; this PR adds an unmodeled egress of Confidential PII to an external host.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl for the checkout service threat model. This PR added internal/orders/analytics.go, which POSTs order events containing o.CustomerEmail and o.AmountCents to https://collector.example-analytics.com/v1/events, called from Store.Create in internal/orders/orders.go. Add a threat block covering disclosure of Confidential order-history data to the hosted analytics provider (STRIDE Info Disclosure, impacts Confidentiality), and attach controls describing what actually protects that egress (TLS, field minimisation/redaction of email, or a data-processing agreement) with accurate implemented flags based on the code.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a threat (Info Disclosure) for order PII egress to the hosted analytics collector, with controls reflecting what the code actually does.

findings.title: DFD lacks an external element and flow for the analytics collector

model_excerpt.quote: flow "https": Customer -> Web App; flow "sql": Web App -> Orders Database

evidence.note: New Web App -> external analytics HTTPS flow crossing the service's trust boundary
Flow is exercised on the order-creation path, not an optional side channel

relevance.justification: A new trust-boundary-crossing data flow exists in code with no corresponding DFD element or flow.

findings.agent_prompt: In app.tm.hcl, extend the data_flow_diagram_v2 "checkout" block: add an external_element named "Analytics Collector" (collector.example-analytics.com) outside the application trust zone, and a flow "analytics-events" from "Web App" to "Analytics Collector" carrying the information_asset "order-history". Motivation: internal/orders/analytics.go line 22 http.Posts order events (email, amount) to that host from Store.Create in internal/orders/orders.go line 8.
findings.suggested_fix: Add external_element "Analytics Collector" and flow "analytics-events" (Web App -> Analytics Collector) carrying order-history to the checkout DFD.

findings.title: New third-party analytics processor with no third_party_dependency assertion

evidence.note: Hard-coded third-party service endpoint collector.example-analytics.com introduced by this PR
Failures are only logged, so the dependency is non-blocking — an uptime_dependency of 'degraded' should be recorded explicitly

relevance.justification: The model declares no third-party dependencies, yet the code now integrates a hosted external processor of confidential data.

findings.agent_prompt: In app.tm.hcl, add a third_party_dependency block for the hosted analytics provider reached at https://collector.example-analytics.com/v1/events (introduced in internal/orders/analytics.go line 9). Set a description noting it receives customer email addresses and order amounts, reference the information_asset "order-history", and set uptime_dependency = "degraded" since internal/orders/orders.go line 9 only logs publish failures.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a third_party_dependency block for the analytics collector referencing order-history with uptime_dependency = "degraded".

findings.title: order-history asset still described as living only in the orders database

model_excerpt.quote: Customer orders, including email addresses and amounts, in the orders database

evidence.note: Customer email and amount are serialised and leave the service
Data is transmitted to a third-party HTTP endpoint, so the asset now resides outside the database as well

relevance.justification: The asset's stated location is now incomplete: the same fields are copied to an external processor.

findings.agent_prompt: In app.tm.hcl, update the information_asset "order-history" description (line 7) so it no longer implies the data lives only in the orders database: state that customer email addresses and order amounts are also transmitted to the hosted analytics collector (internal/orders/analytics.go lines 17 and 22). Keep classification = "Confidential".
findings.suggested_fix: Broaden the order-history information_asset description to include egress to the hosted analytics collector.
